items.title: Put the three parts in order
items.intro: Tap the words to build the Samoan for each English sentence. Two of the words on offer do not belong.

items.why: The particle *sā* comes first, *ia* says she did it, and the verb *tāʻele* comes last.
*ʻOu* is I, and *fāgota* by itself means go fishing.
*Ia* is the pronoun for someone else, and *alu* is go.

items.title: Build the two-participant sentence
items.intro: Tap the words to build the Samoan for each English sentence. Some of the words on offer do not belong.

items.sm: Sā vaʻai le teine i le iʻa.
accept: Sā vaʻai i le iʻa le teine
items.why: The verb comes first, then the one who sees, then the thing seen, marked by *i*. *Sā vaʻai i le iʻa le teine* says the same: the two parts after the verb can come in either order.

items.sm: Sā ʻou vaʻai i le iʻa.
items.why: *ʻOu* keeps its place in the middle slot, before the verb, and the fish still follows with *i*.

items.sm: Sā ia vaʻai i le pusi.
items.why: *Ia* (she) sits before the verb, and *le pusi*, the cat, follows with *i*.

items.sm: Sā ʻou valaʻau i le uō.
items.why: *ʻOu* (I) comes before the verb *valaʻau*, and the one called to follows, marked by *i*.
